Product.P_Desc: An extremely basic browser 'game' built from the ground up to support the Archipelago multi-world randomizer.

FPCMapping.DisabilityImpact: 'Without Vision', 'With Limited Vision', 'With Limited Language, Cognitive, and Learning Abilities'
FPCMapping.TesterComment: Whenever there is a change to the <ul> containing the chests, there is no dialog or alert, and the user's focus is not changed. In addition, the <ul> is not an ARIA live region, nor is it contained in one. I thought it might be bad practice to have such a big aria-live region, so I instead made a separate live region containing toast messages about each change. Maybe I should change this, because even if this is a better option, it's technically a test failure.

SuccessCriteria.RemarkExplntn: 1.2.1-audio-transcript-text. The chest unlock and chest open sound bytes do not have transcripts, but this test doesn't apply to 'short sounds used to notify the user'.
1.3.3-sensory-info. I have not provided any instructions for the game.
2.2.2-Blinking-moving-scrolling. There is automatically moving content, but it stops on its own after less than 5 seconds.
2.4.1-bypass-function. There is repetitive content (the many, many chests), but it doesn't apply to this test because it only appears on one page.
2.4.5-multiple-ways. There is only one web page.

3.1.2-part-language-defined. It's possible for the player or other players to send chat messages in non-English languages, but I don't think that should apply to this test. By default, the web client is entirely in English.
3.2.3-consistent- navigation. There is only one web page.
3.2.4-consistent-identification. There is only one web page.

3.3.4-error-prevention. None of the forms result in any information being saved to a database. Some values are saved in the browser's local storage, but these are not permanent and can always be overridden.

Criteria.DisabilityImpact: 'Without Vision', 'With Limited Vision', 'With Limited Hearing', 'With Limited Language, Cognitive, and Learning Abilities'
Criteria.TestCondition: The user can pause, stop, or control the volume of audio content that plays automatically.
Criteria.TesterComment: If the user wins, a 4-second applause sound will automatically play. However, the win dialog will also be displayed, and the first element the user encounters is its X button. Clicking this button will stop the sound. All other automatically-playing audio is less than 3 seconds long.

Criteria.TesterComment: There is automatically moving content, but it stops on its own after less than 5 seconds.

Criteria.DisabilityImpact: 'Without Vision', 'With Limited Vision', 'With Limited Language, Cognitive, and Learning Abilities'
Criteria.TestCondition: The user can pause, stop, hide, or control the frequency of automatically updating content.
Criteria.TesterComment: The game constantly automatically updates to display collected items/chests, newly unlocked chests, and chat messages. However, automatic updates can be stopped via the 'Disconnect' button, which is the first item in the tab order.

Criteria.DisabilityImpact: 'Without Vision', 'With Limited Vision', 'With Limited Language, Cognitive, and Learning Abilities'

Criteria.TesterComment: Whenever there is a change to the <ul> containing the chests, there is no dialog or alert, and the user's focus is not changed. In addition, the <ul> is not an ARIA live region, nor is it contained in one. I thought it might be bad practice to have such a big aria-live region, so I instead made a separate live region containing toast messages about each change. Maybe I should change this, because even if this is a better option, it's technically a test failure.
